title: Overestimation of racial ingroup worry about the COVID-19 vaccine and medical racism.
summary: We investigate whether there is pluralistic ignorance-a group-level shared misperception of what other group members are doing, thinking, or feeling-around COVID-19 vaccination and medical racism. We focus on two distinct anti-vaccination movements grounded in distinct racial groups: Black Americans and White Americans. Black American vaccine hesitancy is uniquely grounded in the history and continued reality of medical racism. White American vaccine hesitancy is influenced by factors including social media use, institutional mistrust, and psychological reactance. A Qualtrics panel sample (N = 2425) obtained by recruiting 50% Black (n = 1209) and 50% White (n = 1216) Americans were asked how worried they were regarding medical racism, HIV misinformation, COVID-19 vaccine safety, and whether the COVID-19 vaccine was violating individual rights. They were then asked how worried they felt the average White American and average Black American were on these issues. Black Americans had higher levels of worry on all items than White Americans. Among Black participants, there was a consistent pattern of overestimation of other Black Americans' worry across all issues-both COVID-19 related and medical racism related. Among the White participants, overestimation of group worry was only present for the COVID-19 items, not the items relating to medical racism. For both groups, one's own worry about each outcome and exhibiting Actively Open-Minded Thinking were predictors of overestimations of other's worry.

标题：对种族内群体关于COVID-19疫苗和医疗种族主义的担忧的高估
摘要：我们研究围绕COVID-19疫苗接种和医疗种族主义是否存在多元无知——即群体层面对其他群体成员在做什么、想什么或感受什么的共享性错误感知。我们聚焦于两个根植于不同种族群体的反疫苗运动：美国黑人和美国白人。美国黑人的疫苗犹豫独特地根植于医疗种族主义的历史和持续现实。美国白人的疫苗犹豫则受到社交媒体使用、机构不信任和心理抗拒等因素的影响。通过招募50%黑人（n=1209）和50%白人（n=1216）美国人获得的Qualtrics面板样本（N=2425）被询问他们对医疗种族主义、HIV错误信息、COVID-19疫苗安全性以及COVID-19疫苗是否侵犯个人权利的担忧程度。随后，他们被问及他们认为普通美国白人和普通美国黑人在这些问题上的担忧程度。美国黑人在所有项目上的担忧水平都高于美国白人。在黑人参试者中，存在一种一致的倾向，即高估其他美国黑人在所有问题上的担忧——无论是COVID-19相关问题还是医疗种族主义相关问题。在白人参试者中，群体担忧高估仅出现在COVID-19项目上，而未出现在与医疗种族主义相关的项目上。对于两个群体而言，个体自身对每个结果的担忧以及表现出积极开放思维都是高估他人担忧的预测因素。
关键词：多元无知；疫苗犹豫；医疗种族主义；群体担忧高估；积极开放思维

title: Effects of power on emotion and expression during a controversial group discussion
summary: AbstractThe approach/inhibition theory of power proposes that elevated social power increases the experience and expression of positive emotions and that reduced social power increases the experience and expression of negative emotions (Keltner, Gruenfeld, & Anderson, 2003). The evidence to date for these proposed relationships is correlational. Studies that have attempted to find a causal link between power and emotions have failed to do so. The current study manipulated social power in 61 three‐person groups that engaged in a meaningful discussion (explanations for poverty in the US) that produced disagreements and strong emotions. High power individuals experienced and expressed more positive emotions and less anger than low power individuals did. High power individuals were also more likely than low power individuals to openly express their opinions during the group discussion. Implications for theory and future research are discussed. 标题：权力对争议性群体讨论中情绪与表达的影响
摘要：权力的接近/抑制理论提出，较高的社会权力会增加积极情绪的经历与表达，而较低的社会权力会增加消极情绪的经历与表达（Keltner, Gruenfeld, & Anderson, 2003）。迄今为止，支持这些假定关系的证据均来自相关研究。那些试图寻找权力与情绪之间因果联系的研究未能成功。本研究在61个三人群体中操纵社会权力，这些群体参与了一场有意义的讨论（关于美国贫困的解释），该讨论引发了分歧和强烈情绪。高权力个体比低权力个体经历了更多积极情绪、表达了更多积极情绪，并且更少表现愤怒。高权力个体也比低权力个体更可能在群体讨论中公开表达自己的观点。本文讨论了其理论意义及未来研究方向。版权所有 © 2006 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.
关键词：社会权力；情绪；情绪表达；群体讨论；接近/抑制理论
